Methods This qualitative study was conducted within a major Australian healthcare organisation delivering care across three hospital campuses and community-based services. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews were undertaken with staff and representatives across strategic leadership, clinical implementation, research and evaluation, governance and regulation, operational delivery, legal oversight, and consumer engagement. Interviews lasted between 30…

items.title: Face De-Identification: A Domain-Centric Survey From Capture to Processing.
items.summary: Face de-identification (De-ID) aims to remove or conceal personally identifiable facial features in images or videos to prevent identity recognition while preserving utility for downstream tasks. With the rising emphasis on data privacy and responsible AI, face De-ID has emerged as an active research area spanning computer vision and privacy-preserving communities. Early approaches, and many contemporary ones, operate in the digital domain by modifying pixel-level or appearance-level features through post-capture processing. Recent advances extend face De-ID beyond post-processing by integrating privacy mechanisms directly into sensors during image acquisition, bridging sensing systems and…

items.title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non-Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk.
items.summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the…

items.title: Segment anything model (SAM)-driven prompt-guided interactive delineation of gross tumor volume for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy.
items.summary: Background Segment Anything Model (SAM), a prompt-guided foundation model, exhibits substantial potential for medical image segmentation by incorporating prior knowledge through user-defined prompts. However, the application of SAM in radiotherapy target delineation remains limited. Purpose This study proposes a feasible prompt-guided interactive delineation workflow driven by an optimized SAM. Methods A total of 100 rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy cases were collected (60 for training and 40 for testing). This study utilized bounding-box prompts to guide SAM for GTV segmentation. Physicians manually draw box prompts on certain slices, while box prompts for the remaining slices are…

items.title: Hyperbolic Hierarchical 3D Scene Representations for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation.
items.summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation aims to predict 3D objects and their predicates beyond the annotated label space. Compared to closed-set 3D scene graph generation methods, the open-vocabulary approach is more general, practical, and less dependent on labor-intensive ground truth annotations. Existing open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generation methods rely on learning individual object and predicate features in the representation space while ignoring higher-level 3D scene representations, leading to overfitting and suboptimal performance. In this work, we propose a hyperbolic learning-based approach to address this problem by leveraging hyperbolic geometry to learn hierarchical 3D…

items.title: Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody-Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding.
items.summary: Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is crucial for understanding biological function and can accelerate drug discovery efforts. Deep-learning-based cofolding methods such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 can successfully predict many different biomolecular complexes. However, these models show lower success rates in predicting antibody-antigen and molecular glue (MG) ternary complexes, two cases of high relevance to pharmaceutical research. Here, we present sequence scanning, a new workflow, evaluated on Boltz and Protenix, that improves prediction accuracy in these domains by applying systematic constraints to enhance overall sampling diversity. For both use cases, we assess the…

items.title: Two Trees in One Ball, version 4
items.summary: Garrett's tree is built from the six quaternions of norm 5, 1 ± 2i, 1 ± 2j and 1 ± 2k. In the peel coordinate of VOTKP, a step that multiplies a ratio by z has Smith step Γ = (z − 1)/(z + 1) and hyperbolic length ln z, and steps compose by Einstein addition. Read that way, each generator is a Lorentz boost of length ln 5 along its own axis, and the whole tree sits in the Poincaré ball with exact rational coordinates. On the knot side, the Riley meridians of a two-bridge knot on its real curve are boosts of length 2x, and the knot relation closes the word walk into a loop. The paper sets the two trees side by side in one disk: one never closes, the other does. Main results. The ratio-z…

Rhythmic Habitation: AI-Native Furniture, Shared Cognitive Ecology, and the Regenerative Continuum of Living, Working, Playing, and Resting
items.summary: Rhythmic Habitation proposes a research framework for the Aeon Mundi Regenerative Habitation design collection (AREN). It begins with a relational question: how might people, artificial agents, and their shared environment support transitions between focused activity, exploration, restoration, and renewed participation? From this phenomenon, the paper derives the spatial, material, and computational conditions those relationships may require. It does not begin with an existing furniture object and add intelligence to it. The framework connects Shared Cognitive Ecology and the Situated Relational Substrate with a material-first design process. Mycelium-grown composites, stabilized…

Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks for Continuous Motor Control: A Biologically Plausible Model of Motor Cortex
items.summary: Motor cortex acquires skilled movements through recurrent spiking dynamics and experience-dependent synaptic plasticity, yet how such circuits learn continuous motor control using biologically local signals remains unclear. Here, we develop a recurrent spiking neural network model of motor cortex that addresses both the computational and biological requirements of motor learning. We first analytically derived the recurrent firing-rate state directly from synaptic input and trained the network by implicit differentiation, thereby avoiding backpropagation through long spike trajectories. We then introduced State-Carry Initialization, which enables closed-loop motor control by continuously…

items.title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti-Ambipolar Characteristics in n-Type Organic Mixed-Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons.
items.summary: Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio-realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long-term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti-ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti-ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF-ON-OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC…

items.title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
items.summary: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. Finally, we forecast constraints on the couplings for present and future spectroscopic…

items.title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
items.summary: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks…

items.title: Stochastic processes on reductive homogeneous and symmetric spaces
items.summary: In this paper we present a method to effectively and efficiently provide pathwise approximations of the Riemannian Brownian motion on a reductive homogeneous space $M\cong G/H$ endowed with a $G$-invariant metric. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. The efficiency…

items.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
items.summary: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes…

items.title: Scattering of massless scalar waves by higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
items.summary: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. We show that at a fixed frequency, the wave cross…

items.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
items.summary: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the…

items.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
items.summary: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing…

items.title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
items.summary: Scaling humanoid motion foundation models is constrained by the scarcity of diverse, robot-executable data and by the difficulty of jointly learning from heterogeneous multimodal inputs while supporting real-time closed-loop control. We present Movens-5M, constructed from raw Internet videos through clip generation, quality filtering, semantic annotation, motion recovery, and physical refinement with humanoid retargeting and execution verification. It contains 15 million human-motion sequences and 5 million physically executable humanoid-motion sequences spanning over 10,000 hours, aligned with text, RGB video, speech, and music. Building on this data, we introduce Movens-Zero, a scalable…

items.title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the…

items.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
items.summary: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit.…

items.title: From WSIs to Bulk, Spatial and Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: Understanding the spatial distribution of gene expression is key to studying complex diseases like cancer. While Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) and Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scT) provide high-resolution insights, they remain expensive and scarce. In contrast, standard histopathology Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) paired with bulk RNA sequencing are widely available. This work introduces a Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network (GNN) capable of simultaneously predicting bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from WSIs. By extracting morphological features using a Pathology Foundation Model (PFM) (UNI2-h) and constructing spatial graphs at both patch and cell levels, the model learns…

items.title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
items.summary: Recent advances in generative foundation models have expanded the capabilities of embodied AI, enabling increasingly general navigation, manipulation, and long-horizon task execution. However, effective interaction with dynamic environments requires more than only strong perception and reasoning: agents must act with partial knowledge and retain, retrieve, and update information from past observations, actions, and experiences. This survey examines embodied memory as a mechanism for preserving decision-relevant information beyond the current observation. We organize existing approaches along two complementary dimensions: six fundamental memory requirements, spanning world-state…

items.title: Hyperbolic embedding of higher-order simplicial networks
items.summary: Many biological interactions involve groups rather than pairs, as when several proteins assemble into a multi-protein complex. Simplicial complexes naturally capture these collective interactions. Existing hyperbolic embeddings represent network hierarchy and similarity through a few interpretable coordinates, but rely only on pairwise links: they cannot distinguish three units engaged in a common interaction from three units connected only in pairs. We introduce here the hyperbolic higher-order (HHO) embedding, which embeds a simplicial complex into the Poincaré disk, while incorporating its group interactions. The hyperbolic area of the triangle spanned by three interacting nodes then…

items.title: P-generalized determinant over quaternions and its applications
items.summary: This paper introduces the ${\rm P}$-generalized determinant, a more general class of quaternion determinants. It unifies several classical quaternion determinants proposed between 1922 and 2008, including the Moore determinant, the Xie determinant, the Chen determinant, and the Kyrchei row--column determinants, thereby revealing the essential nature of quaternion determinants as multivariate polynomial-type functions with a fixed ordering of products. We provide equivalent characterizations of the expansion of the $\mathrm{P}$-generalized determinant along a given row or column, and establish conversion relations between the $\mathrm{P}_{l}$- and $\mathrm{P}_{r}$-generalized determinants.…

items.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
items.summary: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. Finally, we find general conditions under which phantom-like behavior is possible in…

items.title: Koopman Greedy Spiking Control for Nonlinear Systems under Firing-Rate Limits
items.summary: Neuromorphic controllers interact with physical systems through fixed-amplitude spikes whose timing conveys control information. Existing Lyapunov-based greedy spiking controllers guarantee stability but are restricted to linear systems and neglect firing-rate limits. We extend greedy spiking control to nonlinear systems using Koopman operator theory. For observable dictionaries invariant under differentiation along the input direction, spike-induced state translations admit an exact linear representation in lifted coordinates, enabling exact modeling of spiking jump dynamics. This allows firing decisions to be formulated as comparisons of quadratic Lyapunov functions in the lifted space.…

items.title: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation
items.summary: Patients often arrive at brief, time-constrained clinical visits unsure of what to expect or ask, and millions of adults now turn to general-purpose AI chatbots to prepare beforehand. Yet whether conversational AI improves visit readiness remains unclear. We designed a large language model (LLM)-based visit preparation agent to guide patients before an appointment by gathering clinical context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant health information, building a prioritized list of questions for their clinician, and generating a summary. In a prospective consented randomized study in the Google Health app, 802 U.S. adults held 866 health-related conversations with the visit…

items.title: scAnyOmics: Foundation-Model Distillation for Any-to-Any Completion of Multi-omics Virtual Cells
items.summary: Recent advances in single-cell technologies have enabled the profiling of multiple molecular modalities, including transcriptomics, proteomics, and chromatin accessibility, providing a more comprehensive understanding of cellular states. However, integrating heterogeneous modalities and predicting missing molecular information remain challenging, particularly when paired measurements are limited. Here, we introduce scAnyOmics, a generative framework that distills knowledge from a frozen single-cell foundation model into a multimodal student model. scAnyOmics integrates scRNA-seq, protein-marker measurements, and scATAC-seq into a shared representation, enabling cross-modal prediction and…

items.title: With foundation-model features, aggregator complexity does not improve cross-hospital discrimination in gastric whole-slide image classification
items.summary: Whole-slide image classifiers are usually developed within one hospital and often go untested at unseen hospitals. We assembled 5,036 haematoxylin-and-eosin-stained gastric slides from five Korean hospitals, scanned at 20x and 40x, and compared multiple-instance learning aggregators under leave-one-hospital-out validation on frozen pathology foundation-model features. A hierarchical patch-region-slide graph aggregator (CHIME-MIL) with site alignment and two-scale fusion reached a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.837, above six conventional attention and transformer aggregators trained without these steps. Under a matched recipe it did not exceed…

items.title: Learning from Physical Experience:Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Recent multimodal foundation models exhibit strong perception, reasoning, and in-context learning capabilities, but translating these capabilities into physical action remains challenging. Through real-world experiments across diverse manipulation tasks, we find that ChatGPT-6-Astra, a state-of-the-art general-purpose reasoner, can serve as a physically actionable, context-responsive manipulation policy, demonstrating effective fine manipulation and spatial reasoning. Building on these findings, we introduce LEXP, a harness for learning from physical experience through context-space adaptation. LEXP combines task-level planning with an experience module that interprets execution evidence,…

items.title: Input-dependent Neuromodulation Enhances Mixed-Signal Neuromorphic Hardware
items.summary: Gating mechanisms allow a fixed neural network to adapt its computation to the current input by dynamically modulating its effective parameters. In the brain, neuromodulation uses this principle to move neural circuits between dynamical regimes, and deep learning exploits input-dependent gating, e.g., in gated recurrent networks and self-attention. Input-dependent modulation has also recently been shown to improve spiking neural networks, with particularly strong benefits in small, parameter-limited ones. This makes neuromodulation especially promising for neuromorphic processors at the edge, where area, memory and energy budgets constrain network size, while circuit physics limits…

items.title: Evolution of Financial AI: From Statistical Models to Agentic AI
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) in finance has evolved from statistical learning and machine learning for structured prediction, through deep learning and foundation models for representation learning, language understanding, and reasoning, to retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-grounded reasoning and agentic AI for autonomous planning and execution. In this paper, we examine how researchers and practitioners can select and apply AI methods in finance. We first show that the major paradigms of financial AI address fundamentally different classes of problems, rather than forming a strict hierarchy of capability. We then review the current state of research on AI in finance and trace…

items.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
items.summary: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost? We present TinyAstral, a two-stage approach. We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test. We then freeze the final harness, collect teacher trajectories with reasoning and failure recovery, and distill a small student that…

items.title: QUAL: Quantile Alignment Improves Zero-Shot Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide zero-shot forecasts for unseen series, but their accuracy varies across datasets. Combining several models can reduce this variability, yet zero-shot deployment provides no target labels for selecting or weighting them. We find that a model pool is useful not only as a final ensemble, but also as a probability reference for transforming each member forecast. Aligning quantiles through this pool-relative reference improves every member forecast in aggregate. Motivated by this finding, we propose QUAL (Quantile alignment), a simple label-free framework for improving and combining diverse TSFMs. QUAL first produces aligned member forecasts, then…

items.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling
items.summary: Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. While generative consistency models (CMs) can rapidly estimate Bayesian posterior distributions, they are constrained by type of tracers, kinetic models, and protocols. Training them from scratch whenever a new tracer, model or protocol is used can be computationally intensive. To address this, we introduce LoRACM, a parameter-efficient framework utilizing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to transfer a pretrained foundation CM to novel TB-PET scenarios. We evaluated three adaptation scenarios using simulated and…

items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. Across coding, reasoning and information processing, interactive and embodied tasks, and visual tasks, we trace reported changes…

items.title: Ganoderma lucidum-Driven Fabrication of bagasse-sawdust mycelium-based biocomposites: effects on mechanical strength and water absorption.
items.summary: Mycelium-based biocomposites offer a promising approach to converting lignocellulosic residues into value-added materials. In this study, Ganoderma lucidum was used to fabricate mycelium-based biocomposites from sugarcane bagasse (BMC) and a bagasse-sawdust mixture (BSMC). Different bagasse-to-sawdust formulations were preliminarily screened based on visual assessment of mycelial colonization, and the 10:1 bagasse-to-sawdust ratio was selected for further investigation rather than as an optimized formulation. The resulting composites were evaluated for bulk density, shrinkage, compressive strength, water absorption, structural characteristics, thermal degradation, and soil-burial…

items.title: Vacuum Phase Transition and Decay to Cross the Phantom Divide
items.summary: We show that the vacuum metamorphosis model with decay fits current baryon acoustic oscillation and supernova distance data and cosmic microwave background measurements significantly better than $Λ$CDM and nearly as well as $w_0w_a$CDM with the same number of parameters. Vacuum metamorphosis with decay provides a physically motivated model of dark energy and an explanation of current cosmological data. In this scenario, non-perturbative quantum effects of a massive scalar field freeze the Ricci scalar curvature when it reaches a critical value proportional to the mass squared, inducing a phase transition in the scalar field, giving a phantom dark energy equation of state $w -1$, in…

items.title: Towards Elastic Least Privilege for Agent Planning
items.summary: General-purpose AI agents require authority that changes between tasks and during execution. Common deployments trade broad permissions that expose unnecessary authority and narrow permissions that raise approval requests. Existing mechanisms can enforce dynamic authority, but agent tool interfaces rarely provide the agent's planner, the component that chooses its actions, a means of comparing the authority required by alternative actions or of seeing the cost of the authority it already holds. Drawing on the rich history of access control research, we propose the concept of \emph{elastic least privilege}, in which an agent begins with a small baseline of authority and may acquire more…

items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI). Yet a fundamental question remains: as AI takes on more research tasks, which decisions does it actually control? Even systems that execute entire research workflows may still rely on humans to define research goals, allowable modifications, and criteria for success. Existing taxonomies, typically organized by technique or target artifact, offer limited insight into these differences in research responsibility. This survey presents a unified, control-centered…

items.title: Anomalous Charge Conjugation and Parity in (2 + 1)-Dimensional Relativistic Hydrodynamics
items.summary: We develop a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly involving \( U(1)_Q \), \( U(1)_F \), charge conjugation (acting only on \( U(1)_Q \)), and parity in 2+1 dimensions, characterized by a mutual Chern-Simons level \( k_{QF}=\frac12 \,\,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z) \). Using the established multi-charge anomaly sector, we make explicit that this response is odd under $\mathsf{C}$ and \( \mathsf{P} \) separately but even under \( \mathsf{CP} \), specify a global inflow representative, and derive the equilibrium cross-charge response, including \( \partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4\pi \bmod 1/2\pi \). items.title: Neurodynamical heterogeneous spiking neural network for spatiotemporal cognitive signal processing.
items.summary: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) enable low-power brain-inspired computing via sparse binary spike transmission. Nevertheless, conventional homogeneous SNNs built exclusively upon leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons exhibit limited capacity for complex multi-scale temporal cognitive dynamics. Existing parametric-heterogeneous SNNs only tune internal hyperparameters within single-compartment LIF units and cannot capture diverse neuronal computations observed in biological circuits. Drawing inspiration from cross-neuronal dynamical heterogeneity in neural systems for multi-dimensional perception and cognition, this work proposes the Neurodynamical Heterogeneous Spiking Neural Network…

items.title: The Pauli Spin Algebra, Related Clifford Algebra Representation, and Derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian Operator
items.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Foundations Mechanisms Harnesses and Evaluation
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded robot capabilities, but autonomous execution does not automatically provide autonomous improvement. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) concerns retained changes that can influence subsequent improvement, including the stronger case in which an agent revises the procedures that generate and evaluate future updates. This survey connects large-model learning and reasoning, agent memory and skills, and RSI theory. We compare general agent harnesses with embodied harnesses and organize the literature along four axes: improvement targets, update mechanisms, decision authority and evidence conditions. From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. items.title: Medical superintelligence: foundations and aspirations.
items.summary: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have stimulated discussions about medical superintelligence , yet how to define and evaluate this aspiration remains unclear. We discuss how AI technologies can contribute to more effective care, introducing six interdependent dimensions of medical intelligence to frame contributions of AI to healthcare delivery. As AI capabilities and their integration into clinical workflows advance, improving the quality of care will require more than superhuman performance on isolated tasks. It will require systems that harness AI, independently and in collaboration with humans, to surpass today's strongest human-led health systems in integrated medical…

items.title: The Neutrino as an Open Helical Two-Photon State: Mass Scale, Helicity, and Tetrahedral Leading-Order Mixing
items.summary: Within Delta-c Mechanics the neutrino is proposed to be the same two-photon system as the electron, distinguished by orbital topology: the electron occupies a closed circular orbit, the neutrino an open helix. items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Mechanisms Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. items.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Feral AI and the Emergence of Digital Ecosystems
items.summary: The digital world is approaching a profound phase transition, whose primary drivers, we argue, are different from those that dominate current discussions of AI risk. The transition need not begin with a superintelligent system escaping human control, or with an AI acquiring the ability and motivation to reproduce. Rather, we suggest that it may get under way as AI agents routinely delegate tasks by creating or recruiting other agents. As delegation becomes widespread and recursive, vast numbers of agents will be created; inevitably, some will persist, spread, and create others beyond their original tasks and environments. items.title: Dimensional convergence at the nanoscale: a novel synthesis of experimental evidence justifying direct measurement of quantum coherence in microtubules.
